post.description:
Create a new repository. Provide either `path` (local directory) or `remote_url` (git remote).
When `remote_url` is set, the repository is cloned into ~/git-repos/<name> first,
then the cloned path is registered. Supports https://, http://, git://, ssh://,
ftp://, ftps://, file://, and SCP-style git@ URLs.
When `path` is provided and `auto_init` is true, the directory is created and git-init'd if needed.

header.description:
Header is the optional section heading git appends after the closing "@@"
(usually the enclosing function), with surrounding spaces trimmed.

no_newline.description: NoNewline marks a line followed by git's "\ No newline at end of file".

old_line.description:
OldLine/NewLine are 1-based line numbers, 0 when the line does not exist
on that side (adds have no OldLine, deletes have no NewLine).

is_binary.description:
IsBinary is true only when git reported the file as an actual binary blob
("Binary files ... differ" / "GIT binary patch"). A diff with zero hunks is
NOT necessarily binary — mode-only changes (chmod +x), pure renames and
empty files also produce no hunks. Clients must gate the "can't preview"
message on this flag, never on len(Hunks) == 0.

old_mode.description:
OldMode/NewMode carry the file mode pair when the diff reports one, so a
content-less mode change can be described instead of shown as binary.

old_path.description:
OldPath is the pre-change path, set only for renames and copies (where it
differs from Path). Empty otherwise.

created_at.description: as-provided by source (RFC3339 for GitHub, "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS" for TAPD)

url.description: direct link to the comment in the external UI

current.description:
Current is what the anchored line looks like NOW, when that differs from the
snapshot in Context. Judging "did this actually get fixed?" needs both sides:
Context is what the reviewer commented on, Current is what replaced it. Nil
when the line is unchanged (Context already shows it) or when the anchor is
outdated (there is no current line to show).

current_blob_sha.description:
CurrentBlobSha is the file's blob hash right now; "" when the file is gone
or unreadable. Callers re-pin a relocated comment to it.

issue_count.description:
IssueCount is how many issues currently select this profile. The UI shows
it and refuses deletion while non-zero (design §6.7.4); the server still
enforces the same guard in DeleteProfile.

consumed.description:
Consumed marks a suggestion that a later automatic execution already
absorbed; it is never processed again.

delivery_failed.description:
DeliveryFailed reports that the task/workspace was created and recorded,
but handing the message to its agent failed. The entry still counts as
accepted — the UI warns so the user can open the task manually.

status.description:
Status is the queue-facing state derived from decision+executed:
pending | accepted | ignored. Deriving it keeps the schema unchanged.

enabled.description:
Enabled is the project-wide switch for this source. IM chats still carry
their own mode; a disabled source is off for every one of them.

Enabled is optional: nil preserves the stored value (default true for a
source that has never been configured), so callers that only touch mode
do not silently re-enable a source the user turned off.

paused.description:
Paused is the project-level stop switch: while true the pipeline forces
every source to mode off, so inferred/observe work stops immediately
while explicit requests keep working.

num.description:
Num/Denom carry the sample the value was computed from (e.g. 3 of 12) so
the tile can show a muted ratio without the server sending prose.

unit.description: count | percent | minutes | rounds | tokens | usd

text.description:
Text and URL are source-neutral projections of Payload: adapters keep
their own raw shape (IM marshals Go field names, GitHub the REST JSON), so
the popover reads these instead of guessing keys.

clone_url.description:
CloneURL is the registered repository's git remote, or "" when the repo
has no remote (or is unresolved). The desktop local-runner reads it to
seed-clone an empty bound directory (#478); the SPA ignores it.

current_branch.description:
CurrentBranch is the worktree's own checked-out branch (HEAD). Sourced
from the worktree row directly so it is present even for stale/orphan
associations (the sidebar's repo JOIN would drop those).

browser_cli_login.description:
BrowserCLILogin is true when the server can host an interactive agent-CLI
login inside a browser terminal (GET /ws/cli-login/:tool/terminal). This is
how team-edition users log in: the server runs in a container where the
native-terminal launch used by personal mode is impossible, so the CLI runs
server-side in a PTY and the browser is the terminal (#677). Decorated by
SystemDepsHandler. Admin-only — the SPA also gates the button on role.

personal_mode.description:
PersonalMode is true when niuniu-server runs in personal/embedded mode
(cfg.Auth.Enabled=false). Host-shell ops (open terminal, open path) are
only meaningful in this mode. Decorated by SystemDepsHandler.

installable.description:
Installable mirrors whether Install would actually run a package-manager
command for this tool right now (vs. fall back to a redirect URL). It
captures per-tool nuance the page-level CanInstall cannot:
  - "claude" depends on npm (which ships with node), NOT the OS PM, so
    claude is installable on a LTSC Windows box that has node but no
    winget — even though CanInstall is false.
  - "node"/"python3"/"git" need an OS PM (winget/brew/apt-get).
  - Always false in team edition.
The SPA gates per-tool install buttons on this; CanInstall stays the
page-level "system PM available" signal used by the top-of-page message.

logged_in.description:
LoggedIn reports whether this CLI already has credentials on the server.
Only meaningful for the agent CLIs that have a login flow (claude, codex);
nil for every other tool so the SPA can distinguish "not applicable" from
"applicable but not logged in". Best-effort: on macOS Claude keeps its
token in the Keychain, so a false here can still mean logged-in (see
claudehome.CredsExistInConfigDir).

ahead_count.description: aggregate commits ahead of base across worktrees

created_by.description: creator user ID, nil if NULL

user_message_count.description:
Token usage by type (lifetime, from workspace_stats). Cost in $ is no
longer surfaced (we record tokens, not money).
Aggregate token usage + message counts across the (filtered) set.

anchor.description:
Anchor is the position re-derived against CURRENT content, present on the
list endpoint. Read anchor.status before trusting line_number: "outdated"
means the comment's target is gone and the line must not be rendered as if
it still pointed at the reviewed code.

commit_sha.description:
CommitSha/BlobSha pin the version the reviewer read; ContextLines is the
JSON snapshot of the surrounding source used to relocate the anchor.

resolved.description: Resolved is the REVIEW verdict, independent of SentToAgent (delivery).

side.description:
Side is "old" (a line the diff deletes) or "new" — old-side anchoring is
what makes deleted lines commentable.

totalMatches.description: TotalMatches counts match lines actually returned (post-truncation).

truncated.description:
Truncated is true when results were cut short for ANY reason. Clients must
show this — a silently truncated list reads as "that's all there is".

context_lines.description:
ContextLines is an optional caller-supplied anchor snapshot (JSON). The old
side of a diff isn't in the working tree, so only the client that rendered
the diff can snapshot it; new-side comments omit it and the server snapshots.

side.description:
Side is "old" (a line the diff DELETES) or "new" (default). Old-side is how
a reviewer says "you shouldn't have deleted this" — impossible to express
while comments could only anchor to new-side line numbers.

cli_type.description: CliType picks the agent CLI ("claude" default / "codex").

dir.description:
Dir is the local directory the user picked. Already a git repo => bound
in place; otherwise auto-init'd (with default .gitignore + Git LFS, #233).

workflow_template_id.description:
WorkflowTemplateID optionally pre-selects a workflow (project_templates).
Reserved for the create wizard (#236); not yet consumed server-side.

parent_issue_id.description:
Executable Epic (optional): ParentIssueID attaches this issue as a child of
an Epic (nil = top-level), IssueType is 'task' (default) or 'epic', ExecWave
is the child execution wave.

auto_init.description: Pointer to distinguish between unset and false

cli_type.description:
CliType picks the agent CLI for the workspace. "claude" (default) or
"codex". Empty string normalizes to "claude" in the SQL layer.
Immutable after create: PATCH /api/workspaces/:id rejects this field.

no_repo.description:
NoRepo creates a plain owner-isolated directory with no git worktrees
(office / non-code tasks). When true, Repos must be empty; when false,
at least one repo is required. See docs/architecture/workspace-model.md.

project_id.description:
ProjectID lets the SPA create a project-scoped workspace without binding
it to a specific issue. When set, used to prefill any project-default
scenes (see WorkspaceService.Create scene-layer prefill). Ignored if
IssueID is also set — issue's project takes precedence.

is_studio.description:
IsStudio marks a studio workspace (#232) so the SPA can show the delivery
hint (#238). Omitted (false) for regular workspaces.

repository_id.description:
RepositoryID is set by the studio from-directory flow (#232) so the client
can reference the auto-created/bound repo. Omitted by other create paths.

completion_profile_id.description:
CompletionProfileID is the issue-level completion profile override.
Nil means the issue inherits the project default (§6.5).

exec_status_reason.description:
ExecStatusReason is the human-readable reason behind a terminal exec_status
(blocked-needs-human / abandoned-with-reason, spec §19). Nil when empty.

external_source.description:
External tracker linkage. Empty when the issue is not linked to any
external source. ExternalSource is the provider name (e.g. "github");
ExternalID is canonical ("owner/repo#123"); ExternalURL is the
upstream permalink.

goal_condition.description:
GoalCondition is the per-issue autohost LLM-judge stop condition.
Empty string means "use the workspace-level fallback (or no judge)".

has_workspace.description:
HasWorkspace (spec 2026-09-28 §3 frontend flag): the issue owns a live
(non-archived) workspace, so its parent/child relations are frozen — the
UI hides the parent/child entries the server guardrail would 409 anyway.

parent_issue_id.description:
Executable Epic: ParentIssueID is the parent Epic (nil = top-level),
IssueType is 'task' | 'epic', ExecWave is the child execution wave,
ExecStatus is the Epic execution lifecycle (idle/running/done/failed/paused).

env_provider_group.description: EnvProviderGroup is the provider-group default binding ('' = none).

branch.description:
Branch is the base branch the new worktree forks from. Required so the
server never silently falls back to a guessed default (e.g. "main") that
may not exist in the repo — that fallback used to leave the workspace
shell in place with no worktree on disk and the failure swallowed.

warnings.description:
Warnings carries non-fatal notices from create (e.g. WARN_GIT_LFS_MISSING
when auto-init could not enable Git LFS). Omitted when empty.

resolved.description:
Resolved is the review verdict. Pointer so an omitted field is rejected
rather than silently read as false (un-resolving a comment by accident).

data_dir.description:
DataDir is the niuniu data dir (~/.niuniu), Unix-style. The SPA uses it to
disable selecting this dir or any descendant and to surface an inline
error before submit. The backend enforces the same rule in ValidatePath.

disk_drives.description: Windows drive letters, empty on Linux

home_dir.description:
HomeDir is the directory picker's only default location — the picker must
never open in (or allow selecting) the ~/.niuniu data dir.

completion_profile_id.description:
CompletionProfileID distinguishes three cases: absent (unchanged), null
(clear the override and inherit the project default), or a profile id.
json.RawMessage is required because *int64 cannot tell null from absent.

active_env_provider_name.description:
ActiveEnvProviderName is the provider NAME this workspace's agent
process actually spawned with ('' = none recorded yet). Read-only:
maintained server-side at each spawn.

codex_sandbox_mode.description:
Codex-only fields. Always populated for codex workspaces (defaults
applied if column is empty). Ignored by the SPA for claude workspaces.

env_provider_group.description:
EnvProviderGroup is the provider-group binding ('' = none). Mutually
exclusive with EnvProviderID; the workspace resolves the group's best
usable member in manual order.

env_provider_id.description:
EnvProviderID is the directly-bound subscription-platform provider (issue
#653). nil = no direct binding (env comes from scene/ explicit workspace_env).

is_studio.description:
IsStudio marks workspaces created via the studio "from local directory"
flow (#232). The SPA shows the delivery hint (#238) when true.

issue_type.description:
IssueType is the linked issue's type ('task'|'epic'). Omitted for regular
tasks and workspaces with no linked issue; the SPA renders an Epic marker
in the sidebar only when this is "epic".

parent_issue_id.description:
ParentIssueID is the linked issue's parent (the Epic it belongs to).
Present only when the linked issue is a sub-issue; the SPA renders a
sub-issue marker in the sidebar when this is set.

force.description:
Force skips the per-workspace uncommitted/unmerged change check. When
false, a workspace with changes is reported in `skipped` (reason
"has_changes") instead of being destroyed.

path.description:
Path is workspace-root-relative with forward slashes, e.g.
".worktrees/niuniu-main/internal/api/filetree.go".

repo.description: Repo is the `.worktrees/<name>` subdir, or "" for workspace-root files.

truncated.description: Truncated means this file hit contentMaxPerFile and has more matches.

before.description:
Before/After hold up to `context` lines around the match. The git-grep
fallback cannot label context lines unambiguously, so it returns none.

columns.description:
Columns are [start,end) BYTE offsets of each match within Text, letting
the client highlight the hit. Only ripgrep reports these.

lineTruncated.description: LineTruncated marks a line cut to contentMaxLineLen.

valid.description: Valid is true if String is not NULL
